newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot prods pull back with crude on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot prods pull back with crude on Iraq news.

text.p: U.S. spot gasoline and heating oil prices fell sharply late Friday as NYMEX crude futures slumped on easing tensions in Iraq, players said.
Most gasoline grades gave up about one cent a gallon, and nearly two cents from the session highs after Iraq said it would stop firing at allied warplanes.
But differentials remained stable in both centers -- as they have most of the past week despite volatile movements on the NYMEX screen in reaction to the Iraq drama.

"I thought distillates would have found more support," one Gulf Coast trader said, saying diffs barely budged despite continuing low stocks and exports of several Gulf Coast low sulfur diesel cargoes to Europe in the past ten days.
Prompt Gulf Coast heating oil was offered at about 2.40 cents below the print, steady with Thursday, while low sulfur diesel firmed marginally to about 1.10 cent below the print.
New York Harbor heating oil diffs, meanwhile, firmed about 0.15 cent to 0.05 cent above October futures, players said.

New York summer grade conventional gasoline was seen at one-half cent under the print, stable with Thursday, while higher RVP (13.8-pound) conventional regular was pegged at 1.35 cents under the October screen.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk 212 859-1632
